turns.text:
I’ll query the literature database directly, first checking its schema, then rank qualifying records so 3DCP studies appear first. I’ll keep paper counts distinct from mix records and report only measured published values.
The database contains more than ten exact matches, and the highest-strength qualifying set is entirely from 3DCP studies. I’m checking the associated rheology timing/method metadata and composition records before presenting the ten mixes.
The composition query was rejected because the SQL safety parser treated a semicolon inside the aggregation separator as a second statement. I’m replacing that separator and retrying once.
I found 10 exact matching published mixes. All are from 3DCP studies, representing 10 mix records across 4 papers. Values are reported measurements, not model predictions.

input.sql:
WITH strength28 AS (
  SELECT mix_uid, MAX(CAST(value_canonical AS REAL)) AS strength_mpa
  FROM measurements
  WHERE quantity='compressive_strength'
    AND value_canonical <> ''
    AND age_norm_d <> ''
    AND ABS(CAST(age_norm_d AS REAL)-28.0) < 0.001
    AND CAST(value_canonical AS REAL) >= 40.0
  GROUP BY mix_uid
),
yield_ok AS (
  SELECT mix_uid, MIN(CAST(value_canonical AS REAL)) AS static_yield_pa
  FROM measurements
  WHERE quantity='static_yield_stress'
    AND value_canonical <> ''
    AND CAST(value_canonical AS REAL) BETWEEN 1000.0 AND 4000.0
  GROUP BY mix_uid
)
SELECT
  p.doi,
  p.title,
  p.year,
  p.is_3dcp_study,
  m.mix_uid,
  m.name_in_paper AS mix_name,
  m.system_type,
  m.w_b_reported,
  m.sand_binder_ratio,
  ROUND(s.strength_mpa, 3) AS strength_28d_mpa,
  ROUND(y.static_yield_pa, 1) AS static_yield_pa
FROM strength28 s
JOIN yield_ok y ON y.mix_uid=s.mix_uid
JOIN mixes m ON m.mix_uid=s.mix_uid
JOIN papers p ON p.paper_uid=m.paper_uid
ORDER BY CAST(p.is_3dcp_study AS INTEGER) DESC, s.strength_mpa DESC, CAST(p.year AS INTEGER) DESC
LIMIT 10
